posts.build_brief:
Format: Vertical reel/video (9:16 aspect ratio).

Shot composition: A clinician speaking directly to camera in a calm, clinical setting — warm-lit (soft overhead or side-lit lighting) against a sage or soft grey-blue background. The clinician sits or stands in a relaxed but professional posture, conveying both ease and expertise. The setting feels grounded and editorial (perhaps a naturalistic interior with soft furnishings, a plant, or simple clinical décor), NOT a gym or wellness cliché. Lighting is warm and even — never moody or dark; the authority comes from the speaker's clarity and the clinical credibility of the environment, not atmospheric drama.

No text overlays on the video itself during the talking-head section. Let the speaker carry the hook. At the END of the reel (final frame or last 2–3 beats), introduce a clean, minimal card with:
- Background: Cream or soft warm white, never green-filled.
- Green anchor: A prominent, simple visual — perhaps a subtle geometric element (a horizontal bar, a leaf motif, or a small icon) in #39B54A at the top or side of the card.
- Headline: Satoshi Bold, ~95px+, placed centre-left. ONE meaningful word highlighted in green #39B54A italic (e.g., "Sleep" in green, rest of headline in charcoal).
- Supporting line or stat: Satoshi Medium, ~50px, in charcoal or soft grey, reinforcing the hook (short, punchy).
- Close line: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in green #39B54A, Satoshi Medium, bottom right or centre-bottom.
- Overall feel: Clinical, warm, minimal — never cluttered. The sage/cream palette complements the green anchor without competing.

Reel structure:
- Frame 1 (Hook, 2–3 sec): Clinician speaks the opening hook directly to camera (e.g., "New research shows..."). Warm, conversational, authoritative tone. No overlays.
- Frame 2 (Build, 2–3 sec): Clinician explains the key insight or evidence point. Again, no overlays — the credibility is in the speaker's voice and presence.
- Frame 3 (Payoff, 1–2 sec): Clean transition to the end card (cream bg, green accent, headline, supporting line). Fade or cut cleanly.

Legibility: All reel on-screen text (if any appears on the talking-head section) must be >=36px. The end card headline is ~95px+, supporting line ~50px, close line ~36px. No small print. If the hook is long, shorten it in the script so the speaker lands it in one breath.

New research keeps confirming what we see in the clinic every day: sleep is where the immune system does its most important work.

If you're recovering from viral illness, managing chronic inflammation, or just want to feel more robust — prioritising sleep isn't a luxury, it's clinical medicine.

What's your biggest sleep barrier right now? We can work with that.

Create a CAROUSEL (4 slides) in the structure of a newspaper editorial — reimagined in EHN's green-anchored palette.

**Canvas & Format:** 4-slide carousel (1080 × 1350 px each), 9:16 mobile-optimised.

**Colour Palette:** Cream (#F5F3F0) background with charcoal (#2D2D2D) body text. EHN green (#39B54A) as the dominant visual anchor — use it for the pull-quote box, accent lines, and the doctor's shirt/visual identity. A soft sage green accent (#A8C686) may highlight secondary elements (borders, icons). No competitor blues or newspaper greys — this is warm, clinical, EHN.

**Slide 1 — Hero Announcement (Newspaper Front Page Effect):**
- Background: Cream with a subtle diagonal texture (newsprint grain, very soft, almost undetectable).
- Layout: Position a professional headshot of an EHN clinician (light sage/cream-toned shirt, calm expression, no stethoscope — keep it grounded, not stereotyped) right-of-centre, occupying ~40% of the frame vertically.
- Headline: "Prescriptions rise. Questions don't." in Satoshi Bold, ~95px, charcoal, placed top-left with the word "rise" in EHN green (#39B54A) italic. Keep it short — one meaningful word anchors in green.
- Body copy: 2–3 short lines in Satoshi Medium, ~48px, charcoal, left-aligned, arranged as a newspaper column around the portrait (not filling the entire space — respect whitespace like a Times layout).
- Pull-quote overlay: Large semi-transparent box (EHN green #39B54A background, 80% opacity) positioned centre-right, overlapping the clinician's shoulder. Text inside: "80% more scripts written in 20 years — yet rates of chronic disease haven't dropped." in Satoshi Medium, ~52px, cream text. Clean, bold, readable.
- Close line: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in Satoshi Medium, ~32px, EHN green, bottom-right corner.

**Slide 2 — The Why:**
- Background: White with a thin EHN green (#39B54A) left border (20px wide, full height).
- Headline: "We ask: why?" in Satoshi Bold, ~95px, charcoal, with "why" in green italic.
- Body: Satoshi Medium, ~48px, charcoal. Short statement: "Root cause, not symptom. Nutrition, not band-aid." Flush-left, ample whitespace.
- Icon/visual: A simple line illustration (sage green, #A8C686) of a branching root or upward arrow, subtle, ~150px, positioned right-aligned, lower half.
- Close line: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in EHN green, ~32px, Satoshi Medium, bottom.

**Slide 3 — The What We Do:**
- Background: Cream (#F5F3F0).
- Headline: "Fasting. Nutrition. Movement." in Satoshi Bold, ~90px, charcoal, with "Nutrition" in green italic.
- Body: Three short lines, Satoshi Medium, ~48px, charcoal:
  - "We investigate what your body is telling you."
  - "Then we rebuild from the ground up."
  - "No scripts unless they're part of the plan."
- Visual: A soft, editorial illustration (charcoal line drawing, ~200px) of interconnected health elements (leaf, heartbeat, fork) in EHN green, positioned left.
- Close line: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in EHN green, Satoshi Medium, ~32px, bottom.

**Slide 4 — Call-to-Action / Closer:**
- Background: Charcoal (#2D2D2D) with EHN green (#39B54A) accent bar (30px) at the top.
- Headline: "Book your reset" in Satoshi Bold, ~95px, cream text, with "reset" in sage green (#A8C686) italic for variation.
- Body: Satoshi Medium, ~48px, cream. "Let's find out what your body needs — not what the script pad assumes." Centred, ample breathing room.
- CTA button (visual): A pill-shaped outline in EHN green, ~60px tall, with white/cream text "BOOK NOW" (Satoshi Bold, ~44px). Positioned centre.
- Close line: "Elemental Health & Nutrition" in sage green, Satoshi Medium, ~32px, bottom-centre.

**Overall Feel:** Newspaper editorial authority, rendered in warm creams and greens. Clinician-calm, never sensational. Whitespace-heavy, Satoshi-clean. One meaningful word per headline in green, anchoring the EHN brand throughout. Never the competitor's palette — this is entirely EHN green-forward.

posts.caption:
Your brain keeps meticulous records — and a single poor night's sleep leaves a mark on your glucose metabolism the very next day.

We often think of sleep debt as something that adds up over weeks. But the research is clear: even short-term sleep deprivation can reduce insulin sensitivity and shift glucose regulation, disrupting energy and appetite signals within hours.

If you're noticing energy crashes, intense cravings, or mood swings after a restless night, your metabolic system is trying to tell you something. A functional-medicine approach to sleep (not just sleep *duration*, but sleep *quality* and circadian rhythm) can be a powerful lever for restoring balance.

Sleep matters. It's not a luxury — it's a metabolic necessity.

Ready to explore what's disrupting yours? We'd love to chat.

If you're wired at night — anxious at 10 PM, exhausted but can't settle — your nervous system might need a wind-down ritual that actually works.

Gentle light reduction in the hour before bed isn't just cosy; it signals your body to start shifting from sympathetic (alert) to parasympathetic (rest) mode. That means less cortisol, better melatonin production, and a sleep that feels genuinely restorative.

Try dimming your environment, stepping away from screens, and creating a space that feels safe and still. Your nervous system will thank you.

Ready to rebuild your sleep from the ground up? We're here to help.
